newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates talking to Airbus, Boeing.
newsitem.headline: Emirates talking to Airbus, Boeing.

text.p: Dubai government-owned Emirates airline said on Thursday it was negotiating with Airbus Industrie and Boeing Co for several new aircraft, either Airbus A330s or Boeing 767s.
"We are negotiating with Boeing and Airbus...We've been looking at Airbus 330s and Boeing 767s as well. We have not yet finalised our decision," an Emirates senior spokesman said.
"We expect to sign a deal as soon as a decision is made, which will be shortly," he told Reuters.
The United Arab Emirates daily Arabic newspaper Al-Khaleej on Thursday quoted an unnamed Airbus official in Paris as saying Emirates had concluded a deal for seven Airbus aircraft.
"The negotiations are not completed and no deal has yet been signed," the Emirates spokesman said.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace -- a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Emirates recently took delivery of its third Boeing 777 aircraft. It has another four 777s on firm order and an option for seven more.
Its fleet also includes 16 Airbus A310 and A300s.
